title: Place Value to 1,200: Thousands, Hundreds, Tens and Ones
standard_text: 2.2A use concrete and pictorial models to compose and decompose numbers up to 1,200 in more than one way as a sum of so many thousands, hundreds, tens, and ones; 2.2B use standard, word, and expanded forms to represent numbers up to 1,200
meta_desc: Free Grade 2 place value worksheets for Texas TEKS 2.2A and 2.2B: base-ten blocks, hundreds, tens and ones, expanded form, number names and numbers to 1,200. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Each digit has a place: thousands, hundreds, tens, ones.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Each place is 10 times the place to its right: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands.
  • 1,153 = 1 thousand, 1 hundred, 5 tens, 3 ones.
  • Expanded form adds the value of each digit: 1,000 + 100 + 50 + 3.
  • If there are no tens, write a 0 in the tens place: 1,107.

Examples

Example

4 hundreds, 0 tens, 6 ones

400 + 0 + 6

Answer: 406

Example

1,000 + 100 + 20 + 9

1 thousand, 1 hundred, 2 tens, 9 ones

Answer: 1,129

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Reading the digits in the wrong orderStart with the biggest place on the left.
Writing 1,000 + 100 + 4 as 11,004Each digit goes in its own place: 1,104.
Skipping a zeroNo tens? Write 0 in the tens place.

faq.q: Can a number be shown in more than one way?
faq.a: Yes. 125 is 1 hundred, 2 tens, 5 ones, or 12 tens and 5 ones.
